The Technical Proposal must include a description of the following system components, at a minimum:
Respondents must provide a detailed description of the proposed technology architecture and include one (1) or more diagrams that detail the relationships between key technical components.

Respondents are responsible for delivering a cost-effective, high-availability environment that minimizes the frequency and impact of system failures, reduces downtime, and minimizes recovery time in the event of catastrophic failure.
In this section, Respondents must provide details on their approach to providing a highly available system.
In addition, Respondents must describe their proposed approach to monitoring system performance and use as well as planning, sizing, and controlling the system as capacity needs change.
Respondents must describe how their system manages video uploads when internet connectivity is unavailable or disrupted.
The proposal must explain whether videos are stored locally and automatically uploaded once a connection is reestablished, or if Users are required to manually resubmit.
Respondents should also describe any notifications or safeguards built into the system to ensure no video submissions are lost.
Respondents must provide details on the software and hardware components they proposed for their system.
Respondents should also include details on the tools and utilities used to design, build, test, deploy, report, monitor, and operate the system and its components.
Respondents must describe their approach to integrating the proposed system with other information systems.
Respondents must detail their approach to administering the system and system components.
In addition, Respondents must provide a summary of their proposed strategy for maintaining and repairing the system.

Respondents must provide narrative descriptions of their approach to technical support Services, including 24-hour online support, business-hours telephone support, and processes for handling Service requests and optimization requests.
Respondents must also explain how support staff will be trained to meet HIPAA requirements and how training completion will be verified.
In addition, Respondents must provide a sample Corrective Action Plan template to demonstrate their process for addressing operational deficiencies and system issues.
The Respondent’s approach must clearly show how support and maintenance activities will ensure reliable Service delivery, compliance, and effective issue resolution for both Providers and Clients.
Respondents must detail their approach to security architecture, including the development and implementation measures that will provide security and protection for the system.
Respondents should describe their general approach to reestablishing operations in the event of a catastrophe, as well as their approach to providing HHSC with a disaster recovery plan.
Respondents must provide specifications on any hardware and software components utilized by the proposed security and disaster recovery solutions.
Respondents must describe their proposed methodology for monitoring and reporting system performance, as well as the proposed approach to technology management.
Respondents must address methods for auditing, tracing, and scanning the system, and provide details on the specialized tools they will use to automate and track monitoring and management activities.
Respondents must provide screenshots of the proposed Application to demonstrate system functionality.
Screenshots must illustrate core features such as the Client and Provider interfaces, reporting dashboards, and dose-tracking functions.

Respondents must show how the Application supports medication adherence by allowing Providers to track Client doses, generate summary reports highlighting missed doses, and run dashboards that display compliance information.

These materials must demonstrate that the solution is user-friendly, supports both Synchronous and Asynchronous observation, and provides the tools necessary for monitoring and clinical decision-making.
Respondents must provide at least one sample dashboard screenshot that illustrates how reporting functionality will appear in the Application.
The example should show the ability to track Clients by condition and generate compliance data, including weekly or monthly reporting views.

Respondents must demonstrate how dashboards and reports will be refreshed with current data, role-controlled for appropriate access, and designed to support program monitoring, clinical oversight, and performance tracking.

Respondents must provide narrative descriptions of their proposed transition processes, including how they will coordinate transition activities from Contract award through the Operations Start Date, finalize and update the Transition Plan, and collaborate with the incumbent vendor to ensure an orderly transfer of Services and knowledge.

Respondents must also include a sample Readiness Assessment Plan template to demonstrate how readiness will be measured, along with a narrative description of the process for verifying that all Providers are fully trained on both the mobile and Web-Based Applications prior to go-live.
These submissions must demonstrate the Respondent’s ability to ensure a seamless transition, readiness of systems, and training of end users.
Respondents must provide examples of proposed training materials for both Clients and Providers.

Submissions should reflect multiple formats, including written guides, videos, and web-based modules, and should demonstrate how training will meet accessibility needs, support Users with limited literacy, and be available in multiple languages.

Respondents must also explain how training will be kept current, promptly updated when system changes occur, and delivered in a way that ensures Providers and Clients are confident and proficient in using the system.

Respondents must provide narrative descriptions of their approach to Turnover, including how they will provide weekly status reports during the Turnover Phase, ensure uninterrupted Operations while turnover tasks are carried out, and coordinate activities with DSHS and any successor vendor.
